name: Padjelantaleden Etapp 2: BLT Gisuris/Kisurisstugan - BLT Låddejåhkå/Låddejåkkåstugan

distanceKm.distanceCaveat: STF and BLT/Padjelanta use 23 km. OSM and cropped Naturkartan linework compute about 22.1 km. Preserve the official 23 km until route geometry is normalized and endpoint policy is reviewed.

estimatedTime.naturkartanRelatedSegment: 6-8 hours for Kutjaure-Låddejåhkå, not the full Gisuris-Låddejåhkå stage
fieldReports: Far Far From Home reported Låddejåhkå-Kisuris in about 6h05 on 2023-07-14, reverse direction.
Several reports describe this as a long day even though the walking is mostly nontechnical.
estimatedTime.confidence: high for official time; medium for actual time because weather, wet ground, and ford levels vary

difficulty.label: moderate remote mountain stage
officialClaims: STF calls the terrain relatively easy but identifies this as the longest Padjelantaleden stage.
Naturkartan describes varied surfaces, easy mountain moorland, grassy pastures, willow brush, wet stretches with boardwalks, easy wades, and a steep descent to Låddejåhkå.
keyHazards: Long 23 km hut-to-hut day with no road access.
Three suspension bridges around Varggá/Vuojatädno and possible easy wades.
Vierttjajågåsj near Låddejåhkå can become a meaningful ford after rain.
Open fell sections can be exposed to fog, rain, wind, and poor visibility.
Final approach to Låddejåhkå is steep in the southbound direction.

alternatesAndConnections.name: Kutjaure/Vájsáluokta northern alternate
alternatesAndConnections.description: STF suggests hikers can start at Vájsáluokta, walk to STF Kutjaure, and then continue directly to Låddejåhkå. Naturkartan BD57 covers Kutjaure-Låddejåhkå and joins the Padjelantaleden line for the last 11 km.
alternatesAndConnections.modelingRecommendation: Keep as access/alternate metadata, not part of the official Gisuris-Låddejåhkå stage geometry.

alternatesAndConnections.name: Old/direct Loadásj route
alternatesAndConnections.description: Field reports describe an old route/variant after the Vierttjajågåsj area that may shorten the walk toward Kisuris but is not the official stage line captured in OSM relation 19111627.
alternatesAndConnections.modelingRecommendation: Suppress from import unless a later alternate-route task explicitly researches it.

officialSources.title: STF Padjelantaleden
officialSources.type: official trail overview and stage inventory
findings: Official Swedish stage title is Etapp 2: BLT Kisurisstugan - BLT Låddejåkkastugan.
Distance/time is 23 km and 7-9 hours.

STF describes the stage as the longest on Padjelantaleden, relatively easy southwest walking, three suspension bridges, a climb after the third bridge, views over Vásstenjávrre, and a steep final section down to the cabins.
STF notes the Vájsáluokta-Kutjaure alternative for shortening this long stage.

officialSources.title: STF Padjelanta Trail
findings: English page confirms the stage as BLT Kisuris cabin - BLT Låddejåkk cabin, 23 km and 7-9 hours.
Useful for English app copy but keep Swedish/source spellings in research caveats.

officialSources.title: BLT Gisuris
findings: Gisuris is south of the confluence of Gisurisjåhkå/Kisurisjåkkå and Sjnjuvtjudisjåhkå/Sjnjutjutisjåkkå.
BLT states one cabin has five 4-bed rooms, one 2-bed room and self-catering day room, plus two six-bed cabins, with one open year-round.
Basic sales may include canned/dry food, gáhkku, and fish, but supplies can run out and kiosk payment/currentness must be rechecked.

officialSources.title: BLT Låddejåhkå
findings: Låddejåhkå is north of Låddejåhkå, 500 m west of the bridge on the route between Akka/Vájsáluokta and Stáloluokta.
BLT states 34 beds, one year-round open cabin, self-catering day room, and basic provisions subject to availability.
BLT gives distance to Gisuris as 23 km and to Árasluokta as 12 km.

officialSources.title: Padjelanta.se Låddejåkkå
findings: Gives Låddejåkkå lat/lon as 67.463684, 16.902009.
Confirms distances: Kisuris 23 km, Arasluokta 12 km, Kutjaure 19 km.
Lists summer 2025 dates and prices, which are useful as context but stale for operational import.
officialSources.confidence: high for coordinate and distance; medium for season/prices

officialSources.title: Naturkartan BD57 Kutjaure-Låddejåhkå
officialSources.type: official route description and GPX context
findings: BD57 is not the full official stage 2, but its southern part follows Padjelantaleden for 11 km to Låddejåhkå.
Describes three suspension bridges over Varggá and Vuojatädno, the 100 m last bridge, Loadásj climb, easy wades, reindeer fences, boardwalks, and tent pitches on the island at the Vuojatädno bridges.

officialSources.title: Naturkartan BD58 Vaisaluokta-Akka-Kisuris-Sáluhávrre
officialSources.type: official route description and GPX context
findings: BD58 covers the Gisuris-to-Sáluhávrre part needed for section 2 geometry review, but it includes non-stage northern and continuation coverage.
Use only after cropping and joining with BD57.

officialSources.title: Länsstyrelsen Norrbotten - Aktuellt i fjällen
findings: As of 2026-04-29, no Padjelantaleden stage 2-specific bridge closure was found.
The latest visible 2026-04-22 notice said Länsstyrelsen had stopped checking trails because of unsafe spring snow/ice and rapidly changing water/ice conditions.
officialSources.confidence: high for accessed-date currentness; dynamic source

commuteAccess.summary: This section has no direct road, public transit, ferry landing, or parking at either endpoint. Commute/access records should be modeled as remote gateway metadata rather than endpoint transit stops.

start.name: STF Akka Fjällstuga / Akka helicopter landing
start.operatorNetwork: Fiskflyg scheduled mountain flights; STF hut context
start.caveats: Closest scheduled air access to Gisuris found by the transit lane, but still requires hiking from Akka to Gisuris. Weather can delay/cancel flights; schedule currentness must be rechecked.

start.name: Änonjálmme / Áhkká boat landing
start.operatorNetwork: M/S Storlule / Tjacko AB across Áhkkájávrre/Akkajaure
start.caveats: Boat landing coordinate inherited from section 1 OSM endpoint. The boat can be cancelled by strong wind and does not serve Gisuris directly.

start.name: Ritsem Fjällstation / Ritsem gateway
start.distanceFromEndpointKm: not adjacent; requires boat plus about 16 km walking, or helicopter plus about 14 km walking
start.operatorNetwork: Road to Ritsem / Falcks Omnibus; M/S Storlule; STF/Fiskflyg gateway services
start.confidence: high as a gateway, not as a section endpoint stop
start.caveats: Parking and bus access belong to Ritsem, not to the trail section endpoint.

end.name: Stáloluokta / Staloluokta
end.operatorNetwork: Fiskflyg Ritsem-Stáloluokta and Kvikkjokk-Stáloluokta scheduled mountain flights
end.caveats: Closest regular scheduled transport option found from Låddejåhkå, but it requires hiking about 12 km to Árasluokta plus 10 km to Stáloluokta.

end.name: STF Kutjaure / Guvtjávrre
end.operatorNetwork: STF hut on Nordkalottleden; no confirmed direct 2026 public transport
end.caveats: Closest alternate trail node from Låddejåhkå, but not a true commute endpoint. Keep as access context only.

end.name: Vájsáluokta / Vaisaluokta
end.operatorNetwork: M/S Storlule; Fiskflyg Vaisa/Akka scheduled flights
end.confidence: high as an alternate northern gateway
end.caveats: Farther than Stáloluokta or Kutjaure from Låddejåhkå. It is useful for alternate itineraries, not normal stage 2 endpoint access.

negativeFindings: No bus stop, train station, ferry landing, or parking was found at Gisuris/Kisuris.
No bus stop, train station, ferry landing, or parking was found at Låddejåhkå.

waterSources.summary: Official and field sources indicate frequent mountain watercourses, but water reliability and ford safety vary with rain, snowmelt, and season. Treat hut/stream water as mountain water requiring judgment or treatment.

records.name: Låddejåhkå drinking water
records.reliability: medium-high at hut camp; recheck locally
records.notes: Mapped as drinking water; not independently verified by an official hut page as a tap.

records.name: Running streams and watercourses along stage 2
records.source: Sweden's National Parks service page and Naturkartan BD57
records.notes: Sweden's National Parks says water is generally clear and often drinkable from running streams/watercourses. This is not a guarantee; carry treatment if needed.

records.name: Vierttjajågåsj ford/watercourse
records.notes: Field reports identify this as a recurring ford caution near Låddejåhkå, ranging from easy/boot-off crossing to just below knee after rain. It is not a dependable easy crossing in high water.

camping: Naturkartan says there are good tent pitches on the island at the bridges crossing Vuojatädno.
Naturkartan also says camping can be found on moorland near streams along the route, but this is too general for facility import.
BLT hut camps appear to support tent campers through service fees, but separate tent-area coordinates were not found for Gisuris or Låddejåhkå.
Field reports suggest that tent-place availability can feel uneven around the Loadásj/Låddejåhkå approach, especially in wet conditions.
fire: Do not encode a static fire-allowed flag. Check Länsstyrelsen/Jokkmokk/Krisinformation for current fire bans before any public-facing import.
Laponia/NFS rules prohibit damaging vegetation and taking wood/windfalls; stove-first guidance is safer for app copy.

protectedAreas: Gisuris/Kisuris lies at the meeting context of Sarek, Stora Sjöfallet/Stuor Muorkke, and Padjelanta/Badjelánnda.
Treat the stage as Laponia national-park travel under NFS 2013:10 and current Länsstyrelsen/Laponiatjuottjudus guidance.

dogs.rule: Dogs are prohibited in the Laponia national parks except leashed dogs from 1 January to 30 April.
dogs.importNote: Summer hiking with dogs through this section should be marked not allowed.

dronesAircraft.rule: Aircraft takeoff/landing and low flying require permission; Padjelanta sources summarize drone flying in Padjelanta/Sarek/Stora Sjöfallet as prohibited without permission.

reindeerHerding.rule: Do not disturb reindeer, reindeer gathering/driving, fences, or enclosures. Stage 2 passes reindeer-fence/enclosure context near the route.

fishing.rule: Fishing is generally restricted in national parks. Länsstyrelsen/Jokkmokkskortet 2026 allows fishing within 1 km on both sides of Padjelantaleden in Padjelanta with the correct permit, subject to exceptions including Vuojatädno's eastern shore downstream from Kutjaure.
fishing.importNote: Do not present fishing as generally allowed without permit/rule caveats.

hunting.rule: No hunting in the national parks except for legal/Sámi rights contexts; not relevant as visitor activity.

notes: No current official stage 2 bridge closure was found on 2026-04-29.
The Länsstyrelsen current mountain-condition page is dynamic and must be checked again before publication.
Vierttjajågåsj can be problematic after rain/high water according to field reports and Utsidan.
Assume no mobile coverage along the stage.
BLT says each cabin camp has an open cabin with an emergency telephone connected to police.
Låddejåhkå emergency phone is mapped separately in OSM; Gisuris emergency phone was not found as a separate coordinate.

conditionReports.title: Ultraleicht-Trekking Padjelantaleden 2024
findings: Steep climb immediately after Låddejåhkå in reverse direction.
Vierttjajågåsj ford was the deepest ford of the whole trail after recent rain, just below knee in one spot.
Old Padjelantaleden route branches after the ford and reportedly shortens the route, but the report stayed on official route.
Hillside near Loadásj was increasingly swampy, with boardwalks missing in places.
Fog and heavy rain reduced visibility and comfort; the group used Kisuris hut for drying/overnight.
conditionReports.confidence: high for wet-weather observations; water levels are condition-dependent

conditionReports.title: Far Far From Home Padjelantaleden
findings: Reported 23 km in 6h05 with about 540 m ascent/descent.
Mentions route options after river crossing/steep uphill: shorter over-the-top route or around the mountain following Nordkalottleden.
Describes no difficult river crossings overall, though some required removing boots.
Kisuris brought return to birch trees and mosquitoes.
conditionReports.confidence: medium-high; less granular and may reflect low-water conditions

conditionReports.title: Outdoorseiten Padjelantaleden report
findings: Describes first about 150 m ascent from Låddejåhkå.
Vierttjajågåsj reached after about 1.5 km; direct/old route to Kisuris branches there.
After about 11 km reached the Vuojatädno suspension bridge area where the Nordkalottleden/Kutjaure option connects.
Notes boardwalk over extensive swamp and bad horseflies in unusually hot/dry conditions.
conditionReports.confidence: medium; older report but useful for route structure

conditionReports.title: Wildnis Wandern Padjelantaleden
findings: Describes Gisuris-Låddejåhkå as 22 km, long and easy walking.
Notes the Vuojatädno valley, three suspension bridges, good tent/lunch sites near bridge area, Loadásj climb, views over Vastenjaure and Norwegian mountains, and descent to Låddejåhkå.
Lists no fords for their overview, conflicting with other reports that identify Vierttjajågåsj as a ford caution.
conditionReports.confidence: medium-high for route character; medium for water-crossing statement

conditionReports.title: Utsidan forum note on Vierttjajågåsj
findings: Forum note warns Vierttjajågåsj just before Låddejåhkå can be troublesome in rain/high water and suggests considering a ford a few hundred meters upstream if needed.
conditionReports.confidence: low-medium; older forum source but corroborated by 2024 field report

sourceContradictions.details: STF uses Kisurisstugan and Låddejåkkastugan/Låddejåhkåstugan variants; BLT/Padjelanta commonly use Gisuris and Låddejåhkå; Padjelanta.se uses Låddejåkkå.
sourceContradictions.importImpact: Use a stable section ID and display both variants where useful; avoid treating variants as separate places.

sourceContradictions.details: Official stage distance is 23 km; OSM computes 22.053 km and cropped Naturkartan about 22.154 km.
sourceContradictions.importImpact: Use official 23 km as user-facing value until normalized geometry is reviewed.

sourceContradictions.details: OSM relation 19111627 is per-stage and clean, while Naturkartan requires crops from BD58 and BD57.
sourceContradictions.importImpact: Prefer OSM for stage normalization, cross-check with Naturkartan before drawing/publication.

sourceContradictions.details: Some field reports describe no difficult crossings, while 2024 and Utsidan reports flag Vierttjajågåsj as potentially difficult after rain/high water.
sourceContradictions.importImpact: App copy should mention condition-dependent ford risk rather than promise easy crossings.

sourceContradictions.details: BLT hut pages mention cash-only kiosk payment, while newer price/opening pages may mention card payment. Some pages retain 2025 labels while Padjelanta.se has April 2026 update notes.
sourceContradictions.importImpact: Do not import detailed payment/price/season fields without a fresh operator check.

researchIterations.synthesisDecision: No targeted follow-up batch required before writing. Major import-critical facts are corroborated. Remaining weaknesses are minor facility coordinates, bridge snapping, and currentness checks that can be handled during normalization/publication review.

findings: Main thread verified OSM relation 19111627 via API: 244 nodes, 6 ways, continuous relation, computed distance 22.053 km, max point spacing 419.7 m.
Main thread checked Naturkartan BD57/BD58 GPX whole-file stats and confirmed grouped linework rather than standalone section file.
Main thread checked OSM/Naturkartan/Padjelanta endpoint alternatives for Låddejåhkå and retained Padjelanta.se lat/lon as selected endpoint.
